Persistence fixes and save-reload verification

Book and personal task persistence — verified 12 November 2026

All three findings from the 11 November evaluation are resolved: book chapter changes now save to the database, book comments use real saved records, and PM Today’s Tasks is an account-owned database list. This section supersedes the earlier open Books findings and browser-storage limitation.

Workflow

User enters a chapter, comment or personal task → Server checks account, role, book scope and form data → Database commit → Success feedback on the same page → Reload reads the saved record

Chapters: user instructions

  1. Open Book Projects, choose Table View and select the book. Admin and PM entry points use the same chapter controls and endpoints, with each account’s own navigation.
  2. Where your role permits chapter management, choose Add Chapter. Enter a positive chapter number that is unique in that book, a title, author and status. Select a system author to delegate the chapter, or enter an external author name without creating an account. An internal assignee is checked against the actor’s allowed author list.
  3. Press Save Chapter. The saved row appears and the book’s completion counts refresh. Reload, select the same book and check that the row is still there.
  4. Use Edit chapter to change its title, author, editor or status. Completed chapters update the saved completion count. Delete chapter requires the existing confirmation and updates the database and totals. Deleting a chapter does not reduce the book’s planned chapter target.
  5. Invalid data, duplicate numbers and failed requests keep the modal and entered values visible with an error. The interface updates after a successful database response.

Chapter management retains the Admin, Centre Head, Overseer and PM entitlement boundary, including elevated Staff with Admin permissions. Ordinary Staff and Supervisor authors receive only their assigned chapters and cannot forge chapter changes. Dean has read-only chapter oversight. Financial Admin’s book workspace is limited to assigned book projects and their scoped chapter view. IT and Student accounts are not offered this publication workspace.

Comments: user instructions

  1. On the book card, open the details button, then Comments. Existing comments load from the database; the demonstration comments have been removed.
  2. Enter the comment and press Post Comment. Text, the authenticated author and creation time are saved. Reload the book and reopen Comments to see the saved discussion.
  3. Other accounts with permission for that book can read the discussion. The browser check confirmed that an Admin’s saved review appears for the assigned Financial Admin in a fresh session.

Comments support plain text, up to 10,000 characters. The unused Attach File control was removed. Input is displayed as text, and the server chooses the author from the signed-in account. Empty or oversized comments are rejected without clearing valid entered text.

Today’s Tasks: user instructions

  1. On the PM dashboard, enter a task and press Add. The database records its owner and today’s date in Africa/Johannesburg. Reloading, signing back into the same account or using another browser retrieves the same saved list.
  2. Use Mark as done to save completion, Reopen task to undo completion, and Delete task to remove it. These changes persist after reload.
  3. The list is personal and separate from shared project tasks. Another account cannot list, update, delete or claim your records. Earlier dates remain in the database and are excluded from today’s list.
  4. If old browser-only entries exist, Import previous browser tasks appears. Review the task titles and target account, and confirm only if the list belongs to you. The old list was shared within a browser, so it is never imported automatically.
  5. After a successful confirmed import, those entries are in the current account’s database list and the old browser list is removed. Failed or cancelled imports leave the old list intact. Import supports up to 100 entries, rejects invalid batches atomically, and skips titles already in that account’s list for today to avoid repeat imports.

New personal tasks are not written to browser storage. Reading and removing the legacy key is confined to the optional import. Previously lost in-memory chapters or demo comments cannot be recovered from a database that never received them; verified missing work must be re-entered.

Automated and browser evidence

The final suite passed 361 tests, including 10 added persistence tests with role subcases. Tests cover chapter create/edit/delete/readback, author privacy, validation, cross-centre denial, external author names, completion totals, shared comments, author spoofing, personal task isolation/date filtering, import idempotency/atomicity and protected saves with CSRF checks enabled.

The 11-profile browser journey created and reloaded records, checked completed chapters after edit/reload, confirmed duplicate-number errors retain their input, and deleted/reloaded chapters. It saved and reopened real comments. It also created, completed, reopened and deleted personal tasks with reloads between actions. The PM legacy import was confirmed and verified after reload. No script errors were observed. A separate fresh-session check verified shared discussion between Admin and assigned Financial Admin. These tests used local SQLite data and did not modify production records.

Deployment and migration

Deploy manager/0013_bookcomment_dashboardtask.py with these changes. This additive migration creates manager_bookcomment and manager_dashboardtask and leaves existing book/chapter tables and data in place. It applied successfully to the isolated local database. makemigrations --check --dry-run reports no missing model changes.

The repository’s Render build command already runs python manage.py migrate. Allow that migration to complete before accepting the deployed pages. For another host, run python manage.py migrate --noinput against the intended deployment database before serving the new revision. No new environment variable or salary encryption key is required. Keep the existing salary encryption keys safe as described elsewhere in this manual. Database backups must include the two new tables.

A pushed commit does not establish that Render has finished deploying. Check the build/migration log, then smoke-test one saved chapter, comment and personal task with a reload on the deployed revision. Real SMTP, cloud file storage, PostgreSQL recovery, load, penetration and accessibility checks retain their earlier separate acceptance requirements.

Repeat the automated checks

.venv/Scripts/python.exe manage.py test --settings=project_manage.settings_test --noinput

Always pass explicit test settings when running tests; default settings may target production. See Persistence browser results.json, Persistence role API results.json, Persistence shared comment results.json and Automated test results.txt in this handover folder.
